newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore shares fall, seen higher after holidays.
newsitem.headline: Singapore shares fall, seen higher after holidays.

text.p: Singapore shares closed down below the 2,200 level on Tuesday but were expected to rebound immediately after Chinese Lunar New Year and Muslim Eid Al-Fitr holidays, dealers said.
"There's no deliberate pattern of selling going on," said a local dealer, adding that underlying sentiment remained firm.
"The new issues are doing well, so that's a good sign for the market," he said.
At Tuesday's close the key Straits Times Industrials Index was down 25.84 at 2,192.22 on weak volume of 149.3 million shares producing 198 losers against 155 gainers.
A fall on the Business Times-Singapore Regional Index of 3.61 points saw it close at 1,102.45. Over the counter shares on the UOB-OTC index inched up 1.47 to 1,279.21.
Creative Technology was the largest loser, pulling back from a Singapore $3.00 profit-taking tumble earlier in the day to end down S$2.00 at S$19.00.
Over the counter Malaysian stocks Malayan Banking and Oriental Holdings led gains, up S$0.60 at S$16.20 and S$0.50 at S$12.60 respectively.
